clue.text: Jester to reach princess that's not all there

indicators.note: something not all there is incomplete, so the name loses a letter from its end

parts.note: to come to a place is to reach it
Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A court fool sets out to approach a slightly dotty princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all there' sounds like a remark about the princess's wits, but it is a literal instruction to drop her name's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester was a professional funny man at court, and a comedian is today's paid entertainer who tells jokes.

clue.text: Ubiquitous app in flipping Apple product taking long time

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: the Mac is Apple's computer
an era is a long period of history

explanation.surface: A popular app is found on an Apple gadget that takes ages to load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' just tacks ERA onto the reversed MAC; 'flipping' also reads as a mild British expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly every smartphone ships with a built-in photo-taking program, so this app is found on practically every handset.

clue.text: Family members eating starter of intestines in French accommodation

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: MA (mother) and SON, two relatives side by side

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: Relatives tuck into tripe while staying in lodgings in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family members' is two relatives, a parent and a child, and the single letter is eaten in the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Maison is the French word for a house or home, a place where people live and are housed.

clue.text: Part of shark seen above water: Floridans unsettled

definitions.text: Part of shark seen above water

indicators.note: what is unsettled has been disturbed out of its order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: people from Florida

explanation.surface: Florida beachgoers are rattled at the sight of a shark breaking the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a scene from Jaws, which makes the anagram easy to miss; the fodder is exactly nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular back fin of a shark is what famously cuts through the surface when one swims near the top.

clue.text: Vegetable ingredient in hot cake Harriet baked

indicators.note: baking transforms the ingredients into something new, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vegetable goes into a warm cake that Harriet made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it points to a hidden word, but the answer is an anagram of all fourteen letters of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The tender centre of the globe artichoke is a common cooking component, sold in jars and used in salads and pizzas.

clue.text: Good times! Cool! Result!

parts.note: ups, as in ups and downs
hot means fashionable, just as cool does

explanation.surface: A string of excited exclamations, like someone celebrating a win.
explanation.walkthrough: HOT and cool look like opposites, but both mean trendy here.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the final outcome or consequence of something, which is what a result is.

clue.text: Bread rising at end

indicators.note: in a down clue something rising goes upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a tip is the end of something

explanation.surface: Dough that rises at the last stage of baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' suggests yeast in dough, but it turns AT TIP upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, hollow, leavened loaf from the Middle East and Greece, often split and filled.

clue.text: Smaller-than-usual fish cooked with zeal

indicators.note: cooking changes raw ingredients into a new form, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two sets of letters

explanation.surface: A small portion of fish prepared enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something half-size is made at a reduced scale, noticeably smaller than the standard version.

clue.text: Swallowing last of Cointreau, a sleuth ordered a drink

indicators.note: to swallow is to take in, so an extra letter joins the mix before it is stirred
to order is to arrange, so the letters are put into a fresh sequence
the last of something is its final part, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: final letter of the liqueur's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective downs some orange liqueur and asks for another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like the barroom verb, but it mixes up the letters of A SLEUTH plus the U.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular asks for 'the usual' at a bar, meaning their customary tipple, which the barman already knows.

clue.text: Perhaps driver supports soothing facilities in recreational establishment

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below the others

parts.note: gentle means calming or soothing
the men's is a public toilet, a convenience or facility
a driver is one kind of golf club

explanation.surface: A chauffeur pays for a relaxing spa at a leisure centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist, but it is a golf club, which sits beneath the other parts in this down entry. 'Facilities' is a polite word for toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentlemen's club is a private members' venue for socialising and leisure, a place of recreation.

clue.text: Policeman: 'Two PMs in report'

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so the letters follow the sound

parts.note: Theresa May and Earl Grey were both British prime ministers

explanation.surface: An officer briefs the press on a story involving two prime ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May and Earl Grey were both UK prime ministers; said together they match the French name, with its silent T.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Maigret is Georges Simenon's fictional Paris police detective, a commissaire of the French force.

clue.text: Woman's captivated by philistines: tell everyone

indicators.note: to be captivated is to be held captive, so the name is held within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A woman is charmed by uncultured people and wants to spread the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's' means 'woman is', so the 's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Estelle is a female given name, and crosswords often define a first name simply by its bearer's sex.

clue.text: Month lost in major reversal: Everyman's drunk wine

indicators.note: a reversal turns things back to front, so the word reads the other way
a drink goes inside the drinker, so one part is taken into the other
what is lost is gone, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for month
the setter refers to himself, so Everyman is I

explanation.surface: After a major setback the setter loses a month and turns to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: MAJOR backwards is ROJAM; drop its M for month to leave ROJA, then the setter's I goes inside after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red Spanish table drink named after the region of northern Spain where its grapes are grown.

clue.text: Ignore girls' weapons

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
lasses are girls, chiefly in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to what the girls are armed with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignore' looks like an instruction to the solver; it is CUT, as in giving someone the cold shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword favoured by sailors and pirates, so these are arms for fighting.

clue.text: This pie came in from the cold?

definitions.text: This pie came in from the cold?

parts.words: This pie came in from the cold?
parts.note: surface reading: an echo of the spy novel The Spy Who Came in from the Cold

parts.words: This pie came in from the cold?
parts.note: setter's reading: an Italian pie that is bought chilled from the freezer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie' swaps in for 'spy' in le Carré's title; pizza is Italian for pie, and this one has come out of the freezer.
explanation.definitionFit: Supermarket pizzas are sold deep-chilled and stored in a freezer until baked, so they literally arrive from the cold.

clue.text: Teacher of ape gouged bananas

indicators.note: to go bananas is to go crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ape's instructor gets ripped off over fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the ape's food, but it means crazy and stirs the letters of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolmaster or instructor, often a strict or pedantic one.

clue.text: Tense, following friend with parrots somewhere in C Europe

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so this piece is placed at the end

parts.note: bud is American slang for a friend
to parrot or ape someone is to mimic them
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Nervous after seeing a pal with birds somewhere in central Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrots' reads as birds but is a verb meaning copies; 'Tense' is not nervous but the grammar term, placed last.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the Hungarian capital, a city in the central part of the continent on the Danube.

clue.text: Honour the German books, showing respect

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
die is a German word for the
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Pay tribute to German literature in a respectful way.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British award given by the monarch; NT is the usual crossword abbreviation for the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: An obedient person complies with authority, deferring to it as a mark of regard and dutifulness.

clue.text: Pope's support complete for untrue tale

parts.note: Urban was the name of eight popes
a leg supports a table or chair
to complete something is to end it

explanation.surface: The Pope's backing is total for a made-up story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope's' is possessive in the surface, but it just supplies a papal name; 'complete' is a verb meaning finish.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban legend is a widely circulated but false modern story, often passed on as having happened to a friend of a friend.

clue.text: Give new kit to thief that's upset

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, so in a down clue the letters go bottom to top

parts.note: a looter steals goods

explanation.surface: A distressed robber is handed fresh equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as distressed, but it overturns the thief's word.
explanation.definitionFit: To retool a factory or workshop is to equip it with fresh machinery and implements.

clue.text: University students' education neglected

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
the NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
ED is short for education

explanation.surface: College students complain that their learning has been ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is the National Union of Students, Britain's student body.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unused has been ignored and not put to work, which is what neglected means here.

clue.text: Earls deny rearing cattle

indicators.note: a rearing horse throws itself about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Aristocrats insist they are not raising livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rearing cattle' reads as farming, but 'rearing' stirs the letters and 'cattle' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderneys are a breed of dairy cow from the Channel Island of Alderney, so they are a kind of livestock.

clue.text: Run with stick, heading off to shop

indicators.note: with its head taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a baton is a short stick

explanation.surface: A relay runner sets off with the baton, then breaks off to go to the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' is the definition as a verb: in British slang to shop someone is to inform on them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on a person is to betray them to authority, the same as grassing or informing.

clue.text: Jealous politician

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a member of an environmentalist party

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one envious politician, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word describes envy, and as a noun it names a member of an environmentalist party such as the Green Party.

clue.text: Sportsperson, part of eleven, terminated

indicators.note: a part comes from inside a whole, so the answer sits within the words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A player from a team of eleven has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eleven' suggests a football or cricket team, which makes the horse-riding answer a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a rider who competes in equestrian eventing, combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Soldiers in resistance shunning restraining devices

indicators.note: to shun is to keep away from, so that letter is left out

parts.note: leg irons are shackles for the ankles
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Fighters in the resistance movement refuse to be shackled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers in resistance' reads as partisans, but 'in' is a link and 'resistance' is just R, taken out of the shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: Legions are large bodies of troops, originally the units of the Roman army, so the word means soldiers.

clue.text: Originally, Tethys, Iapetus, Theia and nine siblings?

definitions.text: Originally, Tethys, Iapetus, Theia and nine siblings?

indicators.note: what comes originally comes at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.words: Tethys, Iapetus, Theia and nine siblings
parts.note: the opening letters of the six words

explanation.surface: A roll call of three Greek deities and their nine brothers and sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Tethys, Iapetus and Theia were three of the twelve children of Uranus and Gaia.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth twelve sibling gods ruled before the Olympians, and these three named ones plus nine more make that family.

clue.text: Seaman did what seamen do, we're told: moved using ropes

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: being told is hearing speech, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: sailors go to sea

explanation.surface: A sailor went to sea, and also shinned down rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ropes' fits a sailor's world, but the answer is a climbing descent; abseil is pronounced 'ab-sail'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a cliff or wall by sliding down a fixed line while controlling speed.
